election._note: Scheduled for 24 October 2027; Wikipedia '2027 Swiss federal election'. No national threshold.

dissolution._note: The Federal Council has no power to dissolve the Nationalrat, and there is no provision for early elections at all -- the same fixed, unremovable shape as formation.censure. data.ipu.org, Switzerland National Council oversight page.

upper._note: Standerat, 46 seats, two per canton and one per half-canton regardless of population -- Appenzell Innerrhoden's 16 000 people return one seat where Zurich's 1.5m return two, which is the most extreme small-place weighting in Europe. Art. 148: the two chambers are equal in every respect, so every act needs both and neither can be overridden. Bundesverfassung, Arts. 148, 150 and 156.

head_of_state._note: The presidency of the Confederation is a one-year rotation among the seven Federal Councillors, held this year by the same Councillor already authored as leader -- one office, one name, no separate clock.
head_of_state.title: President of the Confederation

amendment._note: Every constitutional amendment requires a mandatory popular referendum with a double majority of the people and the cantons -- there is no seats-only path at all, so no seat fraction applies. Declared, unresolved: no referendum mechanic exists yet (V1.1f/V1.7), so no amendment names this system in its own `systems` list, the same shape lose_condition: 'never' already uses for Switzerland. Art. 195, Federal Constitution of the Swiss Confederation.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 195: every amendment requires a mandatory popular referendum, so there is no seats-only path at all -- which is why the rule above is referendum_required. The real double majority of the people AND the cantons is reduced to the popular majority alone: this game has no cantons. See docs/referendum-model.md.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Moot, the same way amendment_rule itself is moot: no transition content names directorial_republic in its `systems`, so this is never looked up. Set false rather than true because nothing in this game's model resolves what a Swiss system change would even mean without the referendum mechanic V1.1f/V1.7 defers.

judicial._note: NO judicial review of federal statutes. Art. 190 Cst.: the Federal Supreme Court and the other authorities are required to APPLY federal acts and international law, which is a binding-force clause rather than a grant of review -- cantonal law is reviewable, federal law is not. Bundesverfassung, Art. 190.

formation._note: The Federal Council is elected by the United Federal Assembly for a fixed four-year term under the power-sharing 'magic formula'. It does not depend on parliamentary confidence and cannot be removed by a no-confidence vote. swissinfo.ch 'The not so magical formula'.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 8.1% is Switzerland's own statutory standard rate, the lowest in Europe (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'). Corporate 19.7% is the commonly cited federal-plus-cantonal average combined rate -- used directly rather than revenue-share-scaled from France, because Switzerland's corporate tax revenue is inflated by multinational profit booking relative to its low headline rate, and scaling by revenue share would have overstated it. Income is France's 20 scaled by Switzerland's OECD Revenue Statistics personal-tax-to-GDP share against France's, hence 17. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 31.3% of GDP against France's 57.3% -- the lowest of the ten (countryeconomy.com / Swiss Federal Finance Administration).
